| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | critical |
| Runs in | scan, pack, guard hook, git push check |
| One-line fix | Rotate this key, remove it from the settings file, and load it from an environment variable instead. |

## What it finds

A key written in an agent's settings, permission allowlist or config file, such as
`~/.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`. It also finds a key inside an agent
file that would ship in a package (see [AP006](/agentprint/checks/ap006/)) or sits in a tracked
settings file that a `git push` would send.

Each print shows the line and the key masked, for example `sk-p…(len 56)`.

## Why it matters

A key in a settings file is a key in plain text. Project settings files are often committed,
and package files are public the moment you publish. A published key has to be treated as
stolen.

## How to fix

1. Rotate the key. Revoke it and create a new one with its provider.
2. Delete the key from the file and load it from an environment variable instead.
3. If the file is in a package or in git, remove it there too (see AP006 and AP007).

## Limits

- Pattern-based only. An odd key format can be missed.
- A key hidden on purpose is found too: cut by invisible characters, split into quoted pieces
  joined with `+`, `.` or `..` or written side by side, cut by an empty quoted string
  (`abc""def`), folded over lines (a trailing backslash, a YAML `|` or `>` block), or
  base64-encoded (under 40 characters only when it is one whole key, such as a lone AWS key
  ID). The print says how, for example `sk-p…(len 56) (hidden: folded lines)`.
  `agentprint fix` leaves a hidden key to you.
- When only the first part of a hidden key is found, `fix` masks that part and the rest stays
  in the file; rotate the key and remove the rest by hand.
- Still missed: a hidden PyPI or 1Password service account token longer than about 600
  characters, a key put together while a program runs (from variables, a join or a decode
  call), a key inside an arbitrary script, pieces in backtick template literals, base64 shorter
  than 40 characters that is not exactly one whole key, URL-safe base64, base64 of mostly
  non-ASCII text or wrapped over several lines, text encoded twice, a YAML block header inside
  a JSON string with extra spaces or a comment, and hidden keys past the per-file limits. The
  full list is under [AP001](/agentprint/checks/ap001/).
- A key inside an MCP server entry is reported as [AP005](/agentprint/checks/ap005/) instead, with
  a fix that fits MCP. A hidden key there is still reported here.
- agentprint never uses the key, so it cannot say whether it still works.
